#3605. Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.

It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027. "The long-silent bells of the remote Asylum ring once more - souring the valley below with discordant and unsettling vibrations," the DLC's Steam page describes. "Garish heraldry, hastily stitched by unskilled hands, festoons the hilltop. Deep within the crumbling masonry of the Asylum, frenzied inmates compete in merciless bloodsport with monsters corralled the kingdom over. And to the victors of these debauched contests, the Butcher’s favour: a cure for their madness."

This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system. On your runs you'll need to prepare for the fights ahead, come across "insane enemy combinations never before possible," and spin a fun wheel which nets you prizes like new battle modifiers, charms and jinxes. There's also a new crowd meter, "a unique feature to the Asylum, can grant powerful effects to your team if you cater to the Crowd's demands. Failing to do so will only earn their scorn which raises the stakes and puts your success in jeopardy!"

The Butcher's Asylum also introduces a new playable character, The Ringmaster. You pick her up by winning bouts in the arena, and then you can recruit her in any game mode. She also serves as the narrator for the DLC, likely because of the passing of the main game's narrator Wayne June; Red Hook made clear earlier this year that they would never use generative AI to recreate June's voice, so I'm glad to see they haven't backstracked here.

The world wants me to write more about Grand Theft Auto 6 and I bravely answer "No". Last week, I obtained 50% of the endings available in Queen's Domain, the best videogame to release in the year 2026. The next 50% require, well, a lot of nook-scouring and cranny-uncovering—many more hours of gameplay which I am preserving for myself as a Christmas holiday treat.

And when I do, I suspect I might make a little (just a little) use of this rad Queen's Domain map by a creator called Leny15. Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell.

No, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. It's one thing to wander these maps as a player, it's another to get a totally flexible birdseye view of how dense, twisty and interconnected they are. I will never stop being blown away by how knotty and elaborate this game is; I love it.

I will also never believe I have actually explored all of it. I'll be honest, gang, I really feel like I've plumbed the depths of this game, but this map has entries for areas I ain't even heard of, and even those areas that I have heard of seem to contain secret sub-areas I've barely touched.

My favourite feature of this thing has got to be the ability to upload your save to it, at which point it will give you a completion percentage and tick off the collectibles and secrets you've already attained (reminder that you can download your Steam cloud saves right in your browser). I was heartened to read that I have, it seems, done in about 70% of this game already. I was even more heartened to learn that the remaining 30% seems even stranger, more complicated, and more baffling than all the rest. I can't wait to check it out.

#3603. GTA 6 has a 99 Metascore from critics, but players are review bombing it

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

"Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality."

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

"The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****."

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close."

GTA 6 launched on Thursday for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Earlier today, actor Jesse James Rose revealed the game features the series' first non-binary character.

Seriously, what is going on with this season?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters. We’ve somehow lost four of the biggest, loudest and most vibrant personalities in consecutive weeks, and now, we’re suddenly left with a season that has a few main characters, a couple wacky side characters and a bunch of people who have been consistently deprioritized and underedited throughout the season. What is going on? How many of these castaways can actually even win?

Jeff Probst has said in the past that there’s no one size fits all winner’s edit on Survivor. That’s both true and misleading. The longtime host and showrunner is correct in that the winner gets a different story based on their personality and what happened out there (the underdog, the challenge beast, the social threat, etc), but there is one very consistent pattern we do see: screentime.

I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative. The show goes out of their way to give us their perspective on what’s going on because the ultimate payoff needs to feel earned and it needs to make sense. That’s just storytelling 101. If we want to know, for example, why someone on the jury does or doesn’t vote for them at the end, it helps if we’re given context and confessionals about their relationship.

Unfortunately, with nine players left in Survivor 51, there are a ton of players who just aren’t present enough in the edit to seem like viable winners. Seriously, let’s run them down real quick. Cristian has been a little more prominent lately, but he had two confessionals during the first four episodes combined. Despite allegedly being so close to Sharonda that he told her about Carter’s idol, we haven’t seen that relationship developed in the slightest. This season would make no sense if he won.

It also wouldn’t make any sense if Thien An won. She’s in last place in total confessionals amongst the players left by an absolute mile. Why? I have no idea. She seems to have great social relationships and is an engaging and sometimes cutting confessionalist when she does get a chance to speak, but she’s the least present character in many episodes for unclear reasons. Why would they do that if she won?

Mike and Eric have been much more present parts of the edit, but their storylines have both been about how much everyone else is annoyed with them. Eric has been getting a wacky theater kid edit that has included multiple montages of him talking and everyone else being annoyed by it. There have maybe been ten shots of characters literally rolling their eyes after he talks. Mike is a different version of the same situation. He’s been the subject of numerous confessionals from other players about how he’s a “bottom feeder” and impossible to work with. I don’t see why Survivor would portray its winner that way.

That’s four of the remaining nine players who have seemingly no chance, and I’m not sure Maggie is in a good spot either. She seems to be one of the most well-liked and dangerous players on the entire island. No one would vote for Mike during the Duos Challenge because he was paired with her, and Jelly has dropped confessionals about how she can win if she gets to the end. But the edit also gave her very little credit for Linnea, even though it was her plan, and she has just over half as many confessionals as Jelly does (24 to 46).

That leaves literally four players: Jelly, Devin, Sharonda and Carter. I’d normally write Carter off because he has two episodes with zero confessionals and no player since Survivor 41 has won with even a single zero confessional episode, but as you can see, we’re a little short on viable winner possibilities. I’m out here trying to make excuses for people’s edits and see some silver lining showing why they could win. I think Carter can win. He’s at least been pretty present during the majority of the season. We’ve gotten his viewpoint consistently, and we’ve gotten confessionals from other people that speak of him very highly.

So, yeah, Carter is a maybe, but really, that leaves us with Jelly, Devin and Sharonda. The Helicopter Alliance has been the most consistent narrative throughline of the entire season, which is why it makes sense that these three are at the top of the list. Jelly and Devin have, without question, been the main characters of 52 (at least since Brady left), and they’re dominating in screentime and confessionals at 46 and 45 respectively. That’s twelve more than Eric, who is in third place of those remaining thanks to a bunch of vampire analogies and references to his fiance Gina.

Sharonda is quite a bit behind with 29 confessionals. Like Carter, there are some concerns with her edit, as there have been stretches where she hasn’t been super prominent, but her content has been so overwhelmingly positive that I’m willing to give her a pass. I still consider her a very viable winner at this point, as she should come into further prominence in the edit once the other players find out she’s been secretly working with Devin and Jelly the entire time.

I don’t know who is going to win Survivor 52. There are three, maybe four viable candidates with Maggie and maybe Mike added in there as wild longshots. That’s a really small number of people in play for there being nine castaways left. In fact, it’s starting to feel a little like Survivor 49 where the entire fanbase was convinced one member of the Tres Leches alliance was going to win because they were the only people who seemed viable for like the entire second half of the game (apart from maybe Steven I guess).

Lack of winning edits aside and a few questionable twist-related decisions aside, Survivor 51 has been an absolute banger so far. Fingers crossed it’s able to stick the landing and fulfill its potential to be an all-time great season, whether one of these obvious contenders wins or not.

#3601. "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way": Toby Fox won't tell his team how Deltarune ends until they've built enough of it

"Just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading…"

Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.

Earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief update on the game's next and sixth chapter. That one's apparently now a "structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end," but that doesn't mean it's quite ready for release, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation." I'd expect a 2027 release for this chapter, which is going to be a shorter one too.

But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an update for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end. "Well, we've only just started…," he explains of the progress. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way."

I'm glad they all think it's fun, the wait for me personally certainly ain't. I do wonder if this speaks to a certain anxiety over how the game will shape up. Following the release of chapter five I was subjected to all manner of theories about what's to come by my partner gorging on YouTube videos from folks who mostly just seem quite excited about it all, even if a lot of them sound wrong. So I imagine there must be a little bit of weight to all of those varying expectations.

Fox did note in the newsletter that "unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" so perhaps I'm speaking a load of hogwash! That said, I'm furious that a character called Apple Girlington didn't make it into chapter five, so you can expect to hear from my lawyers, Mr. Fox.

I have been inundated with GTA 6-related advertising over the last few weeks. Every company on the planet has been in my inbox with some kind of press release tying their product to this massive new release - just this morning I was emailed by a bedding company about all the hours of sleep people must have missed out on in order to pull all-nighters in Leonida. But perhaps the most interesting tie-in comes from Pavel Durov, founder and CEO of messaging service Telegram.

Telegram, if you're not aware, is a messaging platform that is best known for its security, driven by end-to-end encryption and self-destructing messages that make it pretty good for keeping information secret. This makes it pretty popular with, say, investigative journalists, but has also given Telegram a bit of a reputation as something that's also a bit handy if you're a career criminal looking to keep people off your trail. Of course, that particular reputation is not something the company's founder and CEO would be keen to lean into. Or so you might think...

Late last night, Durov tweeted that "the least realistic thing about GTA 6 is that Jason and Lucia run a whole criminal operation without a single Telegram group." Now, I get it. I get the desire to seem like you're part of the zeitgeist, like you're linked to this major new cultural touchstone, and to organically tie your product into that conversation. What I don't entirely get is the impulse to say the quiet part out loud.

The least realistic thing about GTA VI is that Jason and Lucia run a whole criminal operation without a single Telegram group.November 22, 2026

If I know that Telegram is probably pretty useful if you want to keep your illicit dealings secret, Durov must definitely know that. However, Durov also has a product to sell and (presumably) a reputation to uphold as a fine, upstanding citizen who definitely isn't making criminals' lives easier. Put aside for now the fact that GTA 6 has a dedicated 'steal this car' app, and I might avoid making the link between the game and my app so explicitly about crime. Especially given that GTA makes up its own parody software companies to ape those in the real world, and you'd think Durov might have decided to sit this one out.

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

"The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or said whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

Unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". Highlight GTA 6 on your home screen, press Options, and choose Check for Update.

#3598. Eldritch Empathy is a Papers Please-esque roguelite about diagnosing cosmic horror creatures and trying not to lose your marbles as you do

Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being."

You kick things off by embodying Eike, a "young woman who has strange dreams and sightings of twisted creatures in the woodlands neighbouring the sleepy Swiss village she lives in." She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods. You need to thoroughly inspect them, using a book to determine what is going on with them and what they need exactly; it's akin to checking the passport rulebook in Papers Please, hence the comparison.

After figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides. You may use care and precision to navigate to the correct corrupted emotion you have identified from your investigation and purify it. You may also use your tools to cause harm. Whatever you choose, your actions will have consequences." Ominous! You can also plan your runs ahead of time, heading down paths that may offer you some boons here and there, like the option to restore a bit of sanity (it's one of those Lovecraftian kind of horror games, as loathe as I am that we still have to reference that guy).

Also be wary of the fact that actions you take out in the woods can affect your home and community. It's a roguelite with consequences! Mwahahha! Looks pretty neat overall, and has some tasty pixel art attached to it too. No release date just yet, but I'd assume it'll arrive no earlier than next year. You can wishlist it right here.

Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek appears to have followed through on their threat to release the executable of the Xbox build of GTA 6 they put into the wild last week, calling it "an early Christmas gift" for followers and explicitly linking the leak to efforts to recreate the game on PC: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects."

Cyberleek released a near-complete build of GTA 6 late last week, holding back only the main exe—the part that makes everything else run, basically—until either their crypto coin achieved a $15 million market cap, or November 23, whichever came first. The crypto missed badly, but time marches on, and so here we are.

The release of the exe, naturally, includes a call for more "donations" in its readme file (via Reddit) which Cyberleek said will go toward a secretive project "for the gamers." They also taunted Take-Two Interactive's efforts to track them down: "Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has."

Leaks in the game industry aren't anything new, but this case is unique: GTA 6, effectively the biggest videogame of all time, still hasn't been announced for PC, as is Take-Two's way. But the advent of AI means the game could be emulated on our platform far more quickly than was possible in the past—some modders estimated it could happen within a week.

One of the leads on the Leonida recomp project predicted that things will start to move quickly from here:

At the same time, Shayder tempered expectations in a message on the Leonida Discord, saying "it will take at least a week" for the project to reach the point where GTA will be playable on PC.

How that unofficial emulated made-with-AI build would compare to the real deal is an open question, and I strongly suspect the answer will be "not well," but even just having something GTA 6-ish playable on PC is a headache that I'm pretty sure Take-Two would rather not have to deal with. I also wonder whether it will prompt Take-Two to release GTA 6 on PC more quickly than it has with previous releases. A rumor to that effect surfaced in October and I had serious doubts, but it's possible that ongoing emulation efforts will expedite its arrival..

#3596. Phasmophobia's next update lets you ask ghosts to throw things and it's out next week

Phasmophobia's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

You'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and new buttons let you quickly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," said Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive."

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

As wild as it is to admit, I resonated with this.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Body is available to stream right now with a Netflix subscription, and when I learned it was about controversy surrounding a Catholic school, I had to check it out. As someone who attended a Catholic grade school and high school, I was eager to see how it was portrayed, and while things were a bit wilder than I remember, the show really nailed two parts.

For those curious but still want to watch for themselves, I'll keep this spoiler-free. All readers really need to know going in is that this series surrounds a Catholic school dance team, and what happens when an initiation prank goes too far and a student's life is in danger.

Project Hail Mary was called "blatant Catholic propaganda," as described by someone who never watched, and similarly, The Body is being vilified by groups of concerned Catholics who have not and likely will not watch it. As someone who did, I'll admit no one should go into this assuming it'll be a family-friendly adventure, but the parts that handle religion are done with lots of care.

I say this, especially, as a person who went through their teenage years in Catholic school. For many, your teens are going to be one of the most rebellious and potentially dangerous times of your lives. Imagine some of the wildest things you did in high school, and now imagine the feeling that you'll be eternally damned for it days afterward.

"Catholic Guilt," they call it, is shown in full effect in The Body. Obviously, there are people in this who deserve to feel guilty, but there are also cases in which we see characters feel immense guilt or shame for things that would otherwise be quite normal today.

Some of this is due to The Body being set in 2004, when things like LGBTQ+ relationships weren't as prevalent in pop culture and were largely frowned upon in Catholic schools. Pregnant teens at my high school weren't allowed to walk to get their diploma at graduation, and I couldn't imagine what would happen if someone were openly gay back then.

And yet these things happened, and these people existed. It's one of the things I love about The Body, and the way it navigates what would undoubtedly be a scary time for those individuals. Again, it was more extreme than anything I dealt with, but I know that feeling of guilt quite well.

I also think The Body does a great job of handling what goes down when something controversial does happen at a Catholic school. I can't get into specifics, but there was a controversy at my school so big that it received national attention, and the fact that it was a Catholic school only amplified the interest and headlines.

The Internet Can’t Stop Talking About People’s Mouths In Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. I Can’t Unsee It

Like the kids in The Body, a number of kids attending were from families of some renown. Families were willing to keep quiet about events occurring to protect their children, and the school was eager to let any controversy fade as quickly as possible.

There's certainly something to the added pressure of a Catholic school striving to be perfect. As The Body points out, any controversy draws the same critics who will immediately point to past incidents highlighted by the movie Spotlight. No one wants to be the person to bring added negative attention to the religion, but at the end of the day it's a high school full of rowdy teens just like any other.

I'm admittedly a lapsed Catholic, but I would say The Body was the best representation in media for the faith since Wake Up, Dead Man. In that, both deal with Catholicism, but not so much that they're openly mocking or blaspheming it. They're stories about the people who practice it, who are imperfect and flawed. I don't think teachers should show it in class, but it is worth a watch for those who are curious.

Check out The Body and other upcoming Netflix shows as 2026 winds down. With the holidays right around the corner, there's nothing like watching something controversial to spark some conversation at the family dinner table!

#3594. Public-access television is born anew in NIGHT EYE TV, a digital goggle box filled with art game curios

I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own shows through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, quickly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed]

In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah says poor management from EA led to BioWare's was shutdown.

Mass Effect and Dragon Age maker BioWare was shut down by EA shortly after the publisher was acquired by a group of private investors. The studio – while beloved for its legendary RPGs across a 30-year history – had faced a ton of issues over its final few years with high-profile titles like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard failing to impress fans. Some pointed fingers at the studio itself for its demise.

Speaking to Pembridge (via PC Gamer) Darrah recalls an unnamed person's read on the situation: "EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself."

He adds, "they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it,'" in regards to EA's approach to BioWare.

"The reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this,'" Darrah explains, "but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options."

He points to BioWare's pivot to the Frostbite engine, Dragon Age 2's breakneck development cycle, and the whole situation with Anthem as things that were brought about by pressure from EA.

"They basically said [you] got to hit your financials. So what are you going to do?" Darrah adds, "Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something."

#3592. Unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has been rated in Korea

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't announced a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming says is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially announced.

If Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

Complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and new skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

#3591. Alt Video is a digital, faux Blockbuster video store that you can fill with movies from your Letterboxd watchlist and Plex server

And you can even watch those movies in-game

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

This is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

There's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in shows or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

Alt Video is currently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"I think the version of BioWare that survives EA better is a version where we drop down to one franchise at a time, maybe just one franchise at all. Maybe we just carve SWTOR off and they become an independent studio within EA, because I don't know how what I'm about to say makes sense if you don't do that. But you ship Mass Effect, you ship Dragon Age, and then one of those wins—I hate this—one of those wins and then you just become a one-project studio. There are lots of studios within EA that did that and it didn't work—they still got murdered in their sleep, so maybe that doesn't work anyway." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Many are asking themselves how a legendary studio like BioWare, which is responsible for staples of the PC gaming genre like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate, alongside Mass Effect and Dragon Age, can be shuttered.

Former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA. Escalating financial pressure led to the poor decisions and subpar games we saw ahead of BioWare's closure. But what if it had all gone differently? Despite everything, Darrah does question whether there was a way for BioWare to survive under EA.

"BioWare's entire existence under EA—it was essentially zero sum, if somebody was getting resources it was coming at the expense of somebody else," Darrah explains. "It's almost like BioWare has run exactly the same way for its entire existence. But the external constraints were different. So in the early days when BioWare needed more people it hired more people. That's like Baldur's Gate 1, Neverwinter Nights, in the early days when we have all these different threads and branches.

"And then in 2007/2008, when the EA constraints come in, the same desires are there, we need more people to ship our games so the way we fix that in that time period is by cutting off all those other branches. So [Jade Empire sequel] Revolver goes away and the Handheld [Development] Group goes away … and so Dragon Age and Mass Effect eats everything."

The alternative? Scaling things down to meet EA's needs. "Budgets keep going up, but we're still not getting bigger… So what's happening is that the walls are closing in and we're trying to be three things [SWTOR, Mass Effect, Dragon Age] and arguably we can only afford to be two things, or one thing." There's no telling whether this would've saved BioWare, but it has worked for other studios.

"Maxis figured out how to live inside of EA and BioWare never did," Darrah adds. Focusing on just one project does seem to be the answer, or at least Darrah believes it has been for Maxis and Battlefield Studios, which both had games that initially underperformed and weren't well received. "If [Battlefield Studios] don't work on Battlefield then you might as well shut the studio down. So they all work on Battlefield 4 and they fix Battlefield 4 and it becomes successful, like very successful after the fact. The Sims 4, same thing."

On the other hand "Mass Effect Andromeda ships and then Dragon Age 4 which has been starving for resources is like 'No, no [the devs] are supposed to come to us. Where are they?' That need to keep them in place isn't there in the same way. So when I say BioWare didn't adapt to EA, that's what I mean."

The 90 Day Fiancé family has sadly lost yet another beloved member. Sheila Mangubat, who appeared on Season 6 of Before The 90 Days, has reportedly passed away at 35. News of Mangubat's passing first arrived via her former fiancé, David Dangerfield, who shared the news with all of his followers by way of a heartbreaking statement.

David, whom viewers saw travel to the Philippines to see Sheila, posted his message on Instagram. Just months after announcing that he and Sheila were back together after an on-and-off romance, David shared the news as follows:

It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines. I am devastated and still trying to process this loss. Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support. ❤️🕊️

Further details about Shelia's passing arrived via 90 Day insider Shabooty, who found a comment from a friend who said she passed away from uterine cancer. It should be mentioned as of this writing, Sheila's family has not confirmed her official cause of death. There was a level of skepticism from others online, given the lack of an official obituary though, so far, reported evidence seemingly points to this information being accurate.

Prior to this news, there was no mention that Sheila was sick or battling cancer. That fact was what apparently sparked the skepticism from fans regarding the initial claims and led to investigations from other accounts.

Two Updates On 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way's Andi And Nigel Have Me More Confused Than Ever About Their Relationship

90 Day Fiancé fans may remember David (who is deaf) finding love with Sheila and traveling to see if a life together was possible. Almost immediately, they were hit with tragedy, as her mother died after falling down a stairwell just hours after his arrival. Because of the tragedy, David and Sheila arguably weren't in the right mindset to really explore a future relationship and talk about the possibility of her being an eventual father to her son, Jhonreil.

There were other issues between the two, such Sheila being unable to understand or speak American Sign Language. Her misunderstanding presented an obvious communication barrier that neither of them considered before becoming involved. Still, they remained together, and it was even rumored ago that Mangubat was pregnant.

Ultimately, David wanted to bring Sheila to the United States with her son to live with him. Unfortunately, there were issues with the K1 visa process, and there were also financial struggles on his own end amid his attempts to get both of them to the US. That situation led to a brief breakup between them in late 2025, but as mentioned, the 90 Day couple later reconciled.

Fellow 90 Day Fiancé cast members reached out to David after he confirmed Sheila's death, including fellow Before The 90 Days Season 6 alum Tyray Mollett. Plenty of fans also expressed their condolences, and I think there was hope that we'd eventually see David and Sheila return in a future season. At this time, their storyline remains available to stream with an HBO Max subscription.

CinemaBlend offers its condolences to Sheila Manguat's family and friends and wishes them well during this difficult time. Here's hoping for more support and love from the 90 Day community as they continue to navigate this sad situation.

#3587. GTA 6 player gets 30-day PSN ban for sharing in-game nudist photo with a friend

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 said they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

"Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found."

In a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety says that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and says Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt

Crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Keep your eyes peeled, and Leonida is a thriving open-world

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 might only have been with us for a few days, but it's clear from the jump that the level of detail in Rockstar's open world is astonishing. So I asked the GamesRadar+ team to document their favorite little features that might escape your attention if you're not looking very closely. From turn-signals to hyper-efficient snacking techniques, and social media to road condition, here's what impressed us the most in our opening few days.

Barely three hours in, GTA 6's reputation system was something I was still getting my head around, but it was already impressing me. In an early mission where I went to collect rent money for Brian, the store owner got mad at me and pulled a baseball bat. Before he could rush me, I pulled out Jason's pistol and he balked at just the sight of the gun, dropping the bat and agreeing to hand over the payment. I love that the game logged that as an illegal activity, but still one that showed restraint, heightening Jason's reputation as a cool, collected, professional criminal. It's a nuance that few RPGs capture so effectively, and I'm looking forward to how it works over the rest of the game.

They say art imitates life, and that's never been truer than seeing Jason Duval take every opportunity to stuff his face and become a munch goblin in GTA 6. Like when I do it, it's to obtain buffs to my health, stamina, and focus, of course. Choking out police security, I take time to pour myself a mug of java, sipping it as I slink behind cover. After a stressful interaction with a neighbour, I double fist her endless fruit bowl as I crunch apples and leave the cores around her kitchenette. The detail is tremendous – with one hand carrying a crate of beer, Jason will open potato chips one-handed with his mouth before pouring a few bites at a time into his beard-framed mouth. That's my move. I couldn't be prouder.

Jasmine Gould-Wilson, Senior Staff Writer

I have a very particular problem with GTA 6's hyper-realistic car damage mechanics. Specifically, they are so realistic that it makes me panic to even be in my car. The slightest ding against a post box results in an ugly dent in the side of my freshly-painted truck, and don't get me started on how bit of bumper-to-bumper action with another car while squeezing my way onto the highway means an unsightly horizontal scrape all down my… whatever part of the car my door is on. I'm not a cars person, okay? I suck at driving in video games and don't even have my license in the real world (partially because I suck at driving in video games). Yet GTA 6 has me feeling incredibly precious about my ride looking beautiful, and I can't stop visiting every pay and spray in town to address even the tiniest nicks of cosmetic damage.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Rockstar has managed to craft a jaw-droppingly realistic world in GTA 6, with gorgeous scenery rich in details that make Leonida feel like a lived-in place. But it's not the graphics that have left me most impressed – it's the devs' attention to detail with the many hilarious Snapmatic shitposts. The in-universe take on Instagram is full of photos and videos from the various residents of Leonida, but the highlights are the ridiculous memes that wouldn't look at all out of place on real-life social media. From "Taco Bomb made me shid my pant" to "do nothing for two hours or straight jork it," an image outside a nursing home captioned "POV: grandma insulted my 6'7 fem-dom goth milk mommy," and Rockstar even parodying the "we got x before GTA 6" memes, I've spent more time scrolling social media in the game over the last day than I have in real life – and, uh, that's saying something. Jason's algorithm is absurd and deeply cursed, and I'm loving it.

I've spent about four hours with GTA 6 so far, and for most of that time, I've been driving. As a bonafide car sicko when it comes to video games, Rockstar's latest is already making my heart go pitter patter. Why? Because I can actually use my car blinkers to indicate when I'm making a turn with the DPad on my PS5 controller. It might sound mundane, but this is a Big Deal to me. It's something I could only dream of when I was cruising around Vice City back in the day, or getting behind the wheel in GTA 5. I've always been one to obey traffic laws in the series, and you better believe I've been stopping at red lights and making way for passing cars. And now I can also indicate each and every turn like a good citizen should? I'm living the dream. What's more, the indicator even automatically switches off when I make my desired turn like a real car. Be still my car-loving heart.

There's a moment in the first chapter where it's time for a party at a local bar, a well-earned celebration in the wake of some good news. Normally this is the sort of thing in a game that'd have me checking my watch and wondering when I can go back to shooting people, but Rockstar's strong writing and character work turn what might've felt like a filler sequence into a moment for developing relationships and story alike (something I can't yet say about the grocery shopping mechanics). But what stuck out for me is just how real it all felt: that one asshole showing up that everybody regrets inviting, the way that people join and split and converge in different groups, the natural rise and fall of energy across the evening. It all ends with a pleasingly solid pool minigame, interrupted by some belligerent drunks who actually snatched my ball off the table as I was about to pot the winning shot, damn it. Alright, now I'm ready to shoot people again.

GTA 6 may be full of thrilling violence and satirical comedy, but my favorite feature so far is its life-sim management elements. Playing as Jason, there's plenty of opportunity to carry out more mundane activities, and the rewards are deeply gratifying. Ahead of Lucia's release from prison, you can repair your home, buy flowers and groceries, and even order a gold necklace to show her how much Jason cares. Lucia's dialogue conveys the character's appreciation, which is nice enough on its own, but the simple act of doing these things also feels good in the moment. Watching Jason roll paint on bare bedroom walls and affix shingles to a leaking roof is soothing, and adds to the sense of immersion because we see the protagonist committing acts of affection that feel real and relatable. I love stealing cars and generally causing mayhem, but I equally enjoy living out more wholesome fantasies in Leonida, and I implore you to do the same.

One of the biggest changes you'll notice in GTA 6 compared to GTA 5 is the ability to choose. Each mission gives you an objective to complete and lets you decide how to do it. Some early-game errands, like rent collection, can get dirty if you really want, though you can also talk people out of making the dumb decision. It's a fresh change that not only takes GTA 6 to the next level but also lets you shape Jason into who you want him to be. I spend my time outside missions being a chill wife guy who fixes up the house and runs errands – so why let a scripted mission run counter to that? My Jason didn't pick that life; it picked him and he's just trying to make it through the best he can.

Obviously there's so much talk about how much of a lived-in world Rockstar Games has created, but one of the ways this has most stuck out to me is through the use of music. Early on I had to head to an artists market to collect some cash from one of Brian's many clientele, but as I parked my car and wandered through the market and heard Elton John's 'I Guess That's Why They Call It The Blues' playing in the distance on a speaker, so instead of immediately walking in to shake down the acid-dealing hippie, I just sort of hung about to listen. I've loved walking into stores to hear a banger playing on their radio, or hanging around areas like that where what song plays gives you a good idea of what the area's culture is like. Perhaps the best use so far has been in the party scene (mentioned above by Joel) where the local band shows up, but instead of just playing licensed music to simulate it, you hear actual covers of classics like Out of Touch by Hall and Oates, to really drive home that local bar feeling.

I've visited Florida quite a bit over the years, but not as a typical tourist. Much of my time there has been spent driving to visit friends who live among the state's smaller towns, and GTA 6 does an incredible job of showcasing just how awful the local roads are. State highways patched over with mismatched blacktop and concrete? Check. Bizarre turn lanes that appear and disappear without a second to get your bearings? Double check. Hastily paved entrances into strip malls that feel like they're going to destroy your car's suspension? Triple check. Leonida has enough similarities to real-life Florida to send a normal driver to a life of crime.

On my Leonida travels, I found a cow that spoke to me. Yes, that sounds insane but I promise it really happened. A runaway pageant cow called Tootsie, dressed in an elaborate red cover, with red bows tied around her ankles, and a fancy flowery hat, made for the hills, leaving me to help the farmer bring her back. I eventually caught up to Tootsie and calmed her down, but then she uttered a chilling "save me". Like Jason, I also physically recoiled at this. I was unsettled for the entire walk back to the farmer, Tootsie now back to regular mooing. Rather than helping the farmer load her into the trailer, I instead shooed Tootsie away, sending her into the sunset. The farmer was - unsurprisingly - livid, saying she wouldn't make it in the wild. I've not seen Tootsie again but I hope she's doing alright.

I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit.

We all knew The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping was going to open to a big number this weekend, but exactly what big meant was unclear. Experts seemed cautiously optimistic it would be over one hundred million dollars at the domestic box office, but it turns out that caution wasn’t needed. Hunger Games not only made $100M, it blew past $100M.

It’ll be awhile before the official final tally is solidified, but the current box office estimates after the grosses on Friday and Saturday have the film earning a whopping $120M this weekend. That’s more than ten times what the second place movie is going to put up, and it’s a reminder that the franchise, despite a disappointing run from the last installment, has a lot of potential left in it.

You can check out the full top ten from the weekend, as per The Numbers. Those figures notably include a decent opening for I Play Rocky considering its budget and a fine enough hold for Johnny Depp’s Ebenezer, which reminded everyone he’s still a bankable star last weekend…

I’ll get to the other movies in a bit, but before that, we need to talk about Sunrise On The Reaping a little bit more. The four initial Hunger Games movies, which were released between 2012 and 2015 all grossed between $650M and $900M at the worldwide box office. They were also collectively a major pop culture force that came up regularly in casual conversation. Unfortunately, 2023’s Ballad Of Songbirds & Snakes, which follows the story of President Snow prior to gaining power, didn’t have the same appeal and grossed less than $350M worldwide.

Many observers thought the franchise was potentially dead after the large dropoff, but Lionsgate made the smart decision to adapt Sunrise On The Reaping, which follows a young Haymitch as he navigates his way through the games back when he was chosen as a tribute. Suzanne Collins’ novel, which was released last year, was very well received by fans, and the adaptation has gotten pretty decent reviews from critics and very strong scores from fans. It’s unclear what might be next for the franchise, but if this box office run has any legs at all, you’d have to imagine Lionsgate is going to be clamoring for Hunger Games content.

I’m not sure I Play Rocky’s $9M and change opening was everything Amazon MGM was hoping for when it greenlit the movie, but there’s some positivity to be had. The film was reportedly made on a budget of around $30M, and there is some serious Oscar buzz about a potential nomination for Best Picture and another for Anthony Ippolito who is terrific as a young Sylvester Stallone.

Fantastic reviews and word of mouth should help it hold strong over the next few weeks. If it’s able to pick up that Best Picture nomination, it should be enough to push the film into a nice little profit and solid win for Amazon and Amazon customers who should get the chance to watch it on the streaming service down the road.

The last bit worth mentioning here is Ebenezer. The film dropped almost sixty percent week over week, but it’s still crossed $30M domestically and clearly has some legs for a longer run. A majority of people who saw the film mentioned Johnny Depp in the exit polls as the reason they came, which should be enough to net him a few big budget movies coming out of this. I’m not saying he’s already back to being the biggest star in the world, but every dollar here helps get him closer to being a fully-fledged A-lister again.

I’ll see you back here next week where we should get a competitive box office that will likely include more strong grosses from Hunger Games, as well as impressive debuts from Disney’s Hexed and Focker-In-Law.

#3584. Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

Original creator Edmund McMillen said he "had no idea [the update] featured generated music in the daily run"

An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

The Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."

Given the new build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have said anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

This isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ update's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

#3583. Over half of all console players active on GTA 6's launch day played it, says Circana

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella said on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active users] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

#3581. Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

621.35 appears not to completely atone for 621.24's sins

Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out."

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by users on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the issue's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

The canceled BioWare RPG inherited quite a mess

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With Mass Effect Universe, BioWare was trying its best to account for all the endings of Mass Effect 3 in a way that preserved player choice and narrative impact but still allowed for a new story to be told.

That's according to Mass Effect: Annihilation writer Catherynne M. Valente, who worked on Mass Effect Universe before BioWare was shut down and its sci-fi RPG series was put on ice. The Annihilation novel was published in November 2018 as part of the Mass Effect: Andromeda extended universe.

Valente discusses her work with BioWare in a Reddit AMA held in support of the Save Mass Effect movement, which has seen fans call for BioWare and/or its series to be revived, and which Valente plugs in her post about the AMA.

One user asked, "How did you and the rest of the team take the endings into account?" as "each one had pretty wildly different outcomes that are hard to reconcile."

Not for the first time, Valente explains that many Mass Effect Universe details are still under NDA and cannot be shared, plus the game was very unfinished and details could shift. But she does dig into the general approach BioWare took with this narrative challenge.

"I don't think it's being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off," she says, "at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel."

As you may have deduced, "that's kind of a tall fucking order," as Valente puts it. BioWare had to ride multiple horses at the same time and get them all to gallop in the same direction.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The search for "an elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible...it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing," she adds.

Valente reflects on the broader fandom surrounding Mass Effect. "It's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices," she says.

She dismisses the argument that BioWare can simply make ME3's Destroy ending canon, noting that some players, including her, feel strongly about the Synthesis ending. So the solution BioWare had arrived at, she suggests, was decidedly not singular.

"We did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she recalls. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that."

She does, however, say more than that. Valente examines the role of narrative sin eater in a post-ME3 world. "I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess..." The worst part is that I've always gotten the impression BioWare wasn't gleefully sowing with the ME3 endings even back in the day – it's just reaping all the way down. Always those darn Reapers.

Nevertheless, Valente maintains that BioWare was in a good position to tackle all this. "That room was *full* of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don't think it could have been in better hands," she says. "We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it."
